images.alt: A sunset framed by trees with a faint crucifixion figure and the printed poem.
images.rights_note: No individual image credit or separate licence is printed. Exported under publisher authorization after whole-article eligibility review. Embedded object 153 at full native 505×685 resolution and source orientation; normalized baseline sRGB JPEG, 72 dpi, no CMYK/inversion or spatial change. The title, poem and colour toning are irreversibly baked into the only source raster; they remain as an explicit unavoidable-overlay exception. Cropping away the poem would cut the central crucifixion figure, so the entire useful original composition is preserved. Separately painted mailing text, publication logo and tiled outer border are omitted. No pixels were generated, inpainted or retouched. Source JPEG contained 1 trailing newline byte after EOI and no JFIF density; normalization removes trailing data and supplies nonzero 72 dpi density.

html:
Then the Jews cried out, "Let God be crucified.
Let God's blood be upon us and on our children."
Then the soldiers took God, and stripped off His clothes.
They put upon God a scarlet robe of mockery.
They pushed a crown of thorns down on God's head.
And placed a reed for a scepter, in God's right hand.
They bowed the knee before God and mocked Him.
They spit upon God's face and smote Him on the head.
And then they lead God away, and crucified Him.
Many that passed by reviled God, wagging their heads.
And there was darkness over all the land.
Then God cried out with a loud voice, "It Is Finished".
